title: Are Mercedes the team to beat in Qatar?
excerpt:
It was a Mercedes clean sweep on Friday at the Qatar Grand Prix, with Kimi Antonelli leading George Russell in a 1-2 formation across both practice sessions – but can the Silver Arrows maintain that form over their rivals heading into Qualifying?

Just how good are Mercedes looking?

It was certainly a noteworthy start for the squad at the Lusail International Circuit – especially for Antonelli, who went fastest in first and second practice despite not getting flying laps in on the soft tyre, with both of his pace-setting times coming courtesy of the medium compound.

title: Leclerc searching for answers after tricky Friday in Qatar
excerpt:
Charles Leclerc was left searching for answers after a difficult opening day at the Qatar Grand Prix, with the Ferrari driver struggling to understand the extent of Mercedes’ advantage.

Leclerc ended both of Friday’s sessions in seventh position, with team mate Lewis Hamilton eighth on both occasions, while an early spin for the former in FP2 resulted in floor damage that required repairs.

Asked to assess his Friday, the Monegasque said: “Honestly, it’s been a very, very difficult day. It’s not that we didn’t try on the soft, we couldn’t improve on our lap time on the medium.

“I lost the car and had some damage, so we had to repair the car, but that was on the first lap of FP2. Then I couldn’t improve, and even on the new soft tyre later on."

He continued: “The feeling is very difficult to get right and not even on the high fuel where we are strong. For now it looks like a very difficult weekend, but we are working hard to try and understand.

“For some reason, Mercedes are so much faster than everybody expected, so the gaps are a little bit strange. There’s something that is the outlier, we just need to find that.”

When asked to expand on his off-track moment in FP2, Leclerc explained: “I tried to go a little bit early on the throttle. It’s a track where there are some corners where you can take a bit more risk because obviously you’ve got a lot of space, and this is one of those, so I tried to go early on the throttle and I lost the car.”

It was an equally challenging day on the other side of the Ferrari garage, with Hamilton having reported issues with the balance of his car during second practice before a loss of power in the closing stages forced the seven-time World Champion to stop on track, bringing out the Virtual Safety Car.

However, Ferrari Sporting Director Diego Ioverno played down concerns over Hamilton’s reliability issue heading into Saturday, although the Italian highlighted the lack of data available to the team following their disrupted running.

“Lewis had a reliability problem that we are investigating,” Ioverno explained. “That is not a concern for tomorrow, but for sure was a concern for the session.

“All in all, not the best day for us. Not so much data to analyse, but anyhow, a long night for us trying to do better tomorrow.”

With just one practice session remaining before Qualifying, Ioverno also outlined the challenges facing Ferrari as they look to close the gap to their rivals.

“The competition seems quite difficult for us so far,” he added. “We’ll try to gather some more data tomorrow in FP3.

“That most likely will be for quali preparation because here is quite a quali-biased event. The others seem strong. We’ll try to do what we can to close the gap... It’s going to be a challenging weekend.”

title: What the teams said – Friday in Qatar
excerpt:
The drivers and teams report back on all the action from Friday practice at the Lusail International Circuit, ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix.

Nov 27, 2026 9:08pm UTC

Mercedes

Antonelli topped the opening session for Mercedes by a decent margin, finishing half a second ahead of his team mate. His lap was set on the mediums, the Italian not able to extract the same pace from the softs. As for Russell, he ran wide like many others as the pack struggled for grip on the slightly dirty racing line.

Neither got a clean lap in on the softs in FP2 thanks to multiple red flags, setting their times on the mediums. But once again Antonelli was on top of the pile, with Russell closing the gap in second.

Kimi Antonelli - FP1: 1:23.217, P1; FP2: 1:23.077, P1

"It was a positive day overall and I felt good in the car from the first laps. We tried a lot of different things across the two sessions, and it was interesting to see how the car reacted to those changes. We gained a lot of understanding today and that should help us as we work through everything overnight and prepare for tomorrow.

"The car has been feeling strong, but there is still a lot of work to do. The front-left tyre is taking quite a lot of energy and that is going to be an important factor through the weekend. It also looks very close at the front. McLaren made a good step between the two sessions, and we know Red Bull are likely to be competitive as well. We need to keep improving overnight and make sure we are ready for qualifying tomorrow."

George Russell - FP1: 1:23.724, P2; FP2: 1:23.204, P2

"Overall, it was a solid Friday. FP1 was a little more difficult and I wasn't completely comfortable with the car, but we made some good changes heading into FP2 and things felt much better from the first lap of the evening session. The car was giving me confidence and that allowed us to have a productive session and put together some competitive laps.

"It's encouraging to see both cars near the top of the timesheets, but we know things can change quickly from Friday to Saturday. McLaren and Red Bull both look competitive and I expect it to be very close tomorrow. We've put ourselves in a decent position though and, if we can make another small step overnight, hopefully we can be in the fight at the front in qualifying."

Andrew Shovlin, Trackside Engineering Director

"It's been one of our better Fridays of the year. The car seemed to be working well out of the box and the lap time was coming quite easily for the drivers on the Medium tyre. We didn't get the most out of the Soft tyre in FP1, but that gave us some useful information heading into the second session. We didn't make any major changes between the sessions and, whilst George was a little happier and Kimi a little less comfortable with his car, the pace still looked strong for both drivers.

"Neither driver completed their Soft tyre laps in FP2 due to the red flags, so we decided to get on with the long run work. The race pace looked reasonable, and we gathered some useful information, particularly around the front-left tyre which is taking a lot of energy around this circuit. That seems to be a common theme up and down the pit lane and, with a bit of tuning overnight, hopefully we can improve the situation for the remainder of the weekend."

LUSAIL CITY, QATAR - NOVEMBER 27: Andrea Kimi Antonelli of Italy driving the (12) Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team W17 in the Pitlane during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Qatar at Lusail International Circuit on November 27, 2026 in Lusail City, Qatar. (Photo by Mark Thompson/Getty Images)

LUSAIL CITY, QATAR - NOVEMBER 27: (EDITORS NOTE: Image has been digitally enhanced.) George Russell of Great Britain driving the (63) Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team W17 on track during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Qatar at Lusail International Circuit on November 27, 2026 in Lusail City, Qatar. (Photo by Pauline Ballet/Getty Images)

McLaren

Piastri got the better of Norris when both ran the hard tyres in FP1, before Norris returned the favour on the softs. McLaren were then one of very few teams who came out early enough to get clean laps in on the C3 rubber in FP2, both drivers able to set a flying lap before the first red flag. That lifted them up the order, Norris winding up third and Piastri fourth.

Their soft tyre laps were still slower than those of Mercedes on the mediums, meaning there is still work to do for McLaren overnight.

Lando Norris - FP1: 1:24.067, P4; FP2: 1:23.522, P3

“Good to be back on track here in Qatar. We’re in a relatively decent position, and our baseline pace looks comparable with Red Bull and Ferrari. There are still things we need to improve, though, and Mercedes look a lot stronger at the moment.

“We estimate we’re around seven tenths off the lead cars, so we know a single change is unlikely to close the whole gap. But we'll put our upgraded floor on tomorrow and see what we can gain. Even a small improvement will help, even if it won't entirely close the gap to the front.”

Oscar Piastri – FP1: 1:24.077, P5; FP2: 1:23.549, P4

“It’s been a decent first day here in Qatar. Our pace looked pretty reasonable overall, and the car feels decent. There are a few things we need to work on in the longer runs, but, generally, it been a good start.

“Mercedes seem to be a step ahead of everyone at the moment, so we’ll need to find a little more pace to be able to catch them. We’ll get our heads down overnight and see what we can do tomorrow.”

Randy Singh , Senior Director, Racing

“It was a very productive day for gathering important information for the rest of the weekend, particularly regarding tyre behaviour. We’ve opted to prioritise the Medium over the Hard for the race because we don’t think there’s a marked difference in terms of degradation, with the C2 delivering better lap times. With the double mandatory pit stop, there will be less need to manage tyre wear, but we’ll have to see how the situation develops with regard to graining: it was a significant factor in the first session, but things had already improved by the second.

“In terms of performance, Mercedes clearly look the favourites: they’re very strong, especially in the high-speed corners of the final sector. As for the rest, I think that we, Red Bull and Ferrari are all very close, as has always been the case this season.

“We’ll have to try to find the right balance between performance on the fast sections and the slow corners, such as Turn 6. Tomorrow we’ll be fitting the underbody introduced in Las Vegas, which should give us a bit more downforce, but to be clear, it won’t be a game changer.”

LUSAIL CITY, QATAR - NOVEMBER 27: Lando Norris of Great Britain driving the (1) McLaren MCL40 Mercedes on track during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Qatar at Lusail International Circuit on November 27, 2026 in Lusail City, Qatar. (Photo by Dom Gibbons - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

LUSAIL CITY, QATAR - NOVEMBER 27: Sparks fly behind Oscar Piastri of Australia driving the (81) McLaren MCL40 Mercedes on track during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Qatar at Lusail International Circuit on November 27, 2026 in Lusail City, Qatar. (Photo by Mark Sutton - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

Red Bull

Hadjar finished third in FP1, giving a good account of himself despite a mishap in the pits where he seemingly left his box fractions of a second before getting the go ahead. The stewards had a look and opted to hand out a fine. As for Verstappen, like his team mate he seemed to struggle with tyre degradation in the first session.

The second session was also eventful, this time Verstappen tangling with Hamilton when the duo were on different programmes late on. The stewards took no further action, as the Dutchman wound up fifth, just ahead of his team mate.

Max Verstappen - FP1: 1:24.133, P6; FP2: 1:23.576, P5

“That was a little bit of a difficult day for us. The overall balance of the car is not quite there yet, which is costing us lap time, so we are not happy. At the moment the Mercedes are pretty far ahead in the short and the long run - hopefully we can close that gap tomorrow. This track is unique and not an easy one to get all the things right, but of course we will try and work hard as always."

Isack Hadjar - FP1: 1:23.878, P3; FP2: 1:23.583, P6

“I think every team is fighting with a lot of balance limitations because of the track characteristics of this circuit. We've been working on finding the right level and continued that into FP2, where we found some improvement. There's still a gap to the leaders as the Mercedes has been extremely strong so far. At the moment, our goal is the second row, but we always make progress right up until Qualifying, so we can't be counted out yet. Definitely a strong first day and there's more to come.”

Pierre Wache, Technical Director

"Our main challenge today was finding the balance that both the drivers were happy with, which is key for this weekend. The understeer was much greater than we expected, particularly in FP1. Max struggled more than Isack in this regard, but we moved in the right direction with both cars for FP2 and made a step forward, although we faced some compromises as a result. There is still a lot of work to do. Mercedes look very strong in the high-speed corners, and it will be a big challenge to match them. We'll focus on ourselves first to ensure we get to where we want to be."

LUSAIL CITY, QATAR - NOVEMBER 27: Max Verstappen of the Netherlands and Oracle Red Bull Racing prepares to drive in the garage during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Qatar at Lusail International Circuit on November 27, 2026 in Lusail City, Qatar. (Photo by Mark Thompson/Getty Images)

LUSAIL CITY, QATAR - NOVEMBER 27: Isack Hadjar of France driving the (6) Oracle Red Bull Racing RB22 Red Bull Ford Powertrains on track during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Qatar at Lusail International Circuit on November 27, 2026 in Lusail City, Qatar. (Photo by Clive Mason/Getty Images)

Ferrari

Leclerc beat Hamilton by a tenth in the first session of the weekend, the duo evenly matched once again. Hamilton did run wide and take out a marker board late on though, that misadventure at least not damaging the car. But the second session did not go to plan for the Scuderia. First, Leclerc spun off into the gravel and damaged his floor. As such, he missed a chunk of the session as the team swapped out that floor for a different one.

Then late on Hamilton parked up with a lack of power, climbing out of the car which had to be recovered. The team could have a late night identifying and rectifying that issue.

Charles Leclerc – FP1 : 1:24.473, P7; FP2: 1:24.099, P7

"Our competitors look very strong, and the gaps we are seeing at the moment are quite unusual. We need to understand where those differences are coming from and what we can do on our side to improve. We’ll analyse all the data tonight and give it everything in qualifying tomorrow."

Lewis Hamilton – FP1: 1:24.575, P8; FP2: 1:24.216, P8

"FP1 was reasonably straightforward and the car felt okay. We made a few small changes going into FP2 but the second session was more challenging and unfortunately we had an issue towards the end of the long run, which brought our session to an early end. We’ll go through everything tonight and see where we can make improvements for tomorrow."

LUSAIL CITY, QATAR - NOVEMBER 27: Lewis Hamilton of Great Britain driving the (44) Scuderia Ferrari SF-26 makes a pitstop during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Qatar at Lusail International Circuit on November 27, 2026 in Lusail City, Qatar. (Photo by Anni Graf - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

LUSAIL CITY, QATAR - NOVEMBER 27: Sparks fly behind Charles Leclerc of Monaco driving the (16) Scuderia Ferrari SF-26 on track during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Qatar at Lusail International Circuit on November 27, 2026 in Lusail City, Qatar. (Photo by Clive Mason/Getty Images)

Racing Bulls

Lindblad bounced back from his Las Vegas disappointment with a strong performance out of the box, finishing in the top 10 in the opening session. Lawson was a little further back after struggling with power issues in FP1. In the second session, Lawson’s PU looked back to full strength and he climbed back into the top 10, beating his team mate by a tenth. That result bodes well for tomorrow, when Racing Bulls will be targeting two Q3 slots.

Arvid Lindblad – FP1: 1:24.601, P9; FP2: 1:24.547, P10

"It was a solid first day here in Qatar. It's a very fast circuit and certainly presents different challenges compared to Las Vegas, but I really enjoyed myself and felt comfortable in the car. The team did a great job in providing a strong baseline setup, so overall I'm quite happy with how things went. That said, the rest of the weekend won't be easy. The race, in particular, is going to be challenging from a tyre management perspective, so we'll need to be very delicate and stay on top of that. I think we're in a good place and I'm looking forward to tomorrow."

Liam Lawson - FP1: 1:25.593, P14; FP2: 1:24.425, P9

"It's been a decent day for us today and we’ve got a fast car, which is positive. We made some big changes in the right direction between FP1 and FP2, which put the car in a good place. We’ll continue to review the data and make any final tweaks to bring it all together. There isn’t a huge difference between the compounds around here, which is likely to play a bigger role in the race than it will tomorrow. The rest of the midfield are looking strong, so we’ll have to see where everyone ends up in Qualifying. I’m looking forward to it."

Alan Permane, Team Principal

"It's been a solid day today. There was a small issue with Liam's Power Unit in FP1, which wasn't responding quite as it should have. However, we cleared that up for FP2 when he was very much back on the pace. We also made some changes to our balance between the sessions, so both drivers ended up feeling much more comfortable. We have plenty of data from today, which we'll analyse over night to see where we can improve ahead of tomorrow. Our long run pace looks very encouraging, so if we can put everything together, we should have a strong race as we continue our fight for P5."

LUSAIL CITY, QATAR - NOVEMBER 27: Liam Lawson of New Zealand and Visa Cash App Racing Bulls prepares to drive in the garage during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Qatar at Lusail International Circuit on November 27, 2026 in Lusail City, Qatar. (Photo by Rudy Carezzevoli/Getty Images)

LUSAIL CITY, QATAR - NOVEMBER 27: Arvid Lindblad of Great Britain driving the (41) Visa Cash App Racing Bulls VCARB 03 RB Ford on track during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Qatar at Lusail International Circuit on November 27, 2026 in Lusail City, Qatar. (Photo by Rudy Carezzevoli/Getty Images)

Alpine

Alpine believe they will be there or thereabouts here with regards the top 10, and that’s how it appeared in the opening session with Gasly in 10th and Colapinto 12th. But disaster struck for the Frenchman in the second session, Gasly getting on the kerbs and losing the rear. It was a high-speed spin, the Frenchman bouncing through the gravel before winding up beached. He missed out on some running as a result, while the team need to assess the damage to his car overnight. Colapinto had a little duel with Russell in FP2, but other than that kept his session clean.

Pierre Gasly – FP1: 1:24.874, P10; FP2: 1:24.764, P12

“Our session came to an early end after the high-speed spin in Free Practice 2. It is never a nice feeling to face the wrong way at those speeds, but it does not happen very often. We have a few things to understand as a team. With the red flag just before my first push lap, we were quite keen to get a run on low fuel under our belts straight away. We had a little more engine power for that lap and we had quite cold tyre temperatures beginning the lap. I entered Turn 14 quite fast, there was a bit more bottoming, and I ran wide onto the kerb and lost it with no chance to recover the car back on to the track. We have a bit of damage to the floor but I am sure we will get everything fixed and prepared for tomorrow. In terms of our running, it appears we are a little behind Racing Bulls again, so we go into the rest of the weekend chasing them. The car felt okay on my laps, a bit of understeer in places, so there are a few areas for us to work on and improve. Hopefully we'll be in the mix for Q3 and put ourselves in a competitive position.”

Franco Colapinto - FP1: 1:25.409, P12; FP2: 1:25.733, P15

“It has been quite an up and down day where we've really struggled with the balance and not yet been able to find a good rhythm around this track. There were a few issues and delays to the session which stopped me from doing some performance laps, so all in all it has not been the easiest of days. Tyre wear seems quite high amongst all teams, which is what we expected heading into the weekend. Even with the limit on the number of laps, wear and degradation will still play a factor here. The performance delta and feeling between the Medium and Soft tyre is something we need to look into, as a lot of teams seemed to extract more performance from the Medium. We are not where we want to be at this stage of the weekend, but there's still time to turn it around and hopefully be more competitive as we head into Qualifying.”

Steve Nielsen, Managing Director

“It has not been our finest day and it is clear our car has a few limitations at this track, especially with its high-speed sequences. Both drivers have not been completely happy with car balance and the car is not quite where we want it to be at this stage. High speed tends to be a weakness of our car and, while we have improved over the season, it still brings difficulties for the drivers as we saw with Pierre at Turn 14, who went off in quite spectacular fashion. We will need to replace the floor as there is quite a big hole in it but, given the speed, it could have been a lot worse. There is some pace in the car and I think we are in a very tight midfield mix all competing for the final spots in Q3. There is a lot of work ahead of us tonight here at the track and back at Enstone on the simulator to see what we can improve with an aim of making the car easier in the high-speed flow for both drivers.”

LUSAIL CITY, QATAR - NOVEMBER 27: Pierre Gasly of France driving the (10) Alpine F1 A526 Mercedes gets out of his car after spinning off track into the gravel during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Qatar at Lusail International Circuit on November 27, 2026 in Lusail City, Qatar. (Photo by Rudy Carezzevoli/Getty Images)

LUSAIL CITY, QATAR - NOVEMBER 27: (EDITORS NOTE: A special effects camera filter was used for this image.) Franco Colapinto of Argentina driving the (43) Alpine F1 A526 Mercedes on track during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Qatar at Lusail International Circuit on November 27, 2026 in Lusail City, Qatar. (Photo by Mark Sutton - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

Audi

Audi had a quiet opening hour of practice, with their drivers evenly matched but not quite fast enough to make the top 10. They split strategies, the only team to do so with Hulkenberg running the hards and Bortoleto the mediums. As such, the Brazilian was the only driver on the hards in FP2, as Hulkenberg swapped to the mediums. But in terms of the results, it was more of the same, both drivers just outside the top 10.

Nico Hulkenberg – FP1: 1:25.437, P13; FP2: 1:24.871, P13

“A fairly straightforward Friday for us, clean for the most part. Qatar is a very different circuit to what we've had recently, with plenty of high-speed corners, so there's quite a bit to take in and understand. We'll go through everything overnight, see where we can make some improvements and put together a good plan for tomorrow. The field looks as tight as ever, so the small details will make the difference."

Gabriel Bortoleto - FP1: 1:25.053, P11; FP2: 1:24.614, P11

“It was a positive Friday. We had a clean day and I felt I put together some good laps. We still need to find a little more pace to put ourselves in the mix, and everyone here and back at the factories is pushing hard to find it. Track position is especially important here, so we need a strong qualifying and a setup that helps us look after the tyres in the race."

LUSAIL CITY, QATAR - NOVEMBER 27: Nico Hulkenberg of Germany driving the (27) Audi F1 Team R26 and Gabriel Bortoleto of Brazil driving the (5) Audi F1 Team R26 on track during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Qatar at Lusail International Circuit on November 27, 2026 in Lusail City, Qatar. (Photo by Mark Sutton - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

LUSAIL CITY, QATAR - NOVEMBER 27: Sparks fly behind Gabriel Bortoleto of Brazil driving the (5) Audi F1 Team R26 on track during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Qatar at Lusail International Circuit on November 27, 2026 in Lusail City, Qatar. (Photo by Mark Sutton - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

Williams

Both Albon and Sainz had moments in FP1, running wide and kicking up plenty of dust. The team used the session to test out things for 2027, rather than chase lap time. They also had moments in FP2, neither keeping their laps entirely tidy as more and more gravel was kicked up onto the track. Despite the difficult conditions, they managed plenty of laps with Albon once again the pick of the duo on Friday.

Alex Albon - FP1: 1:25.692, P16; FP2: 1:25.276, P14

“It was a difficult Friday as the tyres are tricky, so I think it is maybe the same for everyone. The long run is the focus because the graining is difficult for all cars, and it won't go away. Hopefully we can come up with some solutions and ideas for tomorrow. The qualifying car and the race car need completely different things, so it's going to be a very hard compromise to achieve both, but we'll give it a go.”

Carlos Sainz – FP1: 1:25.992, P18; FP2: 1:25.839, P16

“We had a relatively straightforward Friday today. This track doesn't generally suit our car and it’s a tricky balance for everyone between pushing on this rougher surface and preserving the tyres. We were struggling with balance across the lap which caused some snaps in different corners, but with some fine tuning I think we can extract a bit more from the car. We’ll work on it overnight to get us in a good place for qualifying tomorrow.”

Paul Williams, Chief Trackside Engineer

“I think this weekend is going to be dominated by graining; we saw in FP1 it was harsh on the front left tyre, through Turns 4 and 5 and then particularly into the sequence of 12, 13 and 14. We changed our approach a little bit into FP2, limited the low fuel running and then really tried to maximise the learning on the high fuel. The tyre compounds are the same for everybody; we just need to manage that as best we can. Coming to this circuit, we knew that it was going to be more challenging than last week with the medium-high speed corners here. We've got some work to do this evening and a few other setup changes that we've got in mind, and we'll put the best car out tomorrow that we can.”

LUSAIL CITY, QATAR - NOVEMBER 27: Carlos Sainz of Spain driving the (55) Williams FW48 Mercedes on track during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Qatar at Lusail International Circuit on November 27, 2026 in Lusail City, Qatar. (Photo by Mark Thompson/Getty Images)

LUSAIL CITY, QATAR - NOVEMBER 27: Alexander Albon of Thailand driving the (23) Williams FW48 Mercedes on track during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Qatar at Lusail International Circuit on November 27, 2026 in Lusail City, Qatar. (Photo by Anni Graf - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

Haas

Bearman said the team might struggle here, the track not suiting the car. Both drivers were down the order in FP1, but at least Camara got plenty of laps in and experienced more usual track conditions as he continues to learn what he can about the VF-26. It was much of the same for the team in the second session, Camara again shading his team mate as Haas experimented with their own ‘flip-flop’ rear wing. It remains to be seen whether they will use that for the rest of the weekend.

Oliver Bearman - FP1: 1:25.766, P17; FP2: 1:25.996, P18

“It was a tough day to be honest, we really struggled to find a good balance with the car on both low and high fuel. It felt like we made a bit of progress by the time FP2 came around, the lap that I was doing on softs before the red flag finally felt decent. On high fuel, we carried over some of the damage that I did to the tire in run one, with graining. I think the car is definitely better than it was in FP1, we’re making progress, so we’ll see what tomorrow holds.”

Rafael Camara - FP1: 1:25.685, P15; FP2: 1:25.962, P17

“We had two clean sessions and were able to run through the program and do everything we wanted. Overall, we learned a lot for tomorrow and it was very productive. It’s not an easy track, but every session I get more used to it all and you can take a bit more risk, especially with the wider run-off areas here. We need to keep working and try to improve the car, and on my side there are a lot of things to see as well – so we’ll keep working and be ready for what comes next.”

Ayao Komatsu, Team Principal

“It’s been a challenging Friday, as the car’s limitation is very different here from any other track. In FP1, I think we were too far away on car set-up, but both drivers managed what they could, and we improved the car for FP2 – Ollie, especially, was happier. Across the garage, we tried a few different things, and I think we could learn from each other. We still need to improve things, but I feel a lot better after FP2. We need to work on race pace, we have some work to do there, but it was trouble-free, and we got all the data, so time to get to work.”

LUSAIL CITY, QATAR - NOVEMBER 27: Oliver Bearman of Great Britain driving the (87) Haas F1 VF-26 Ferrari on track during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Qatar at Lusail International Circuit on November 27, 2026 in Lusail City, Qatar. (Photo by Mark Sutton - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

LUSAIL CITY, QATAR - NOVEMBER 27: Rafael Camara of Brazil and Haas F1 is interviews after practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Qatar at Lusail International Circuit on November 27, 2026 in Lusail City, Qatar. (Photo by Anni Graf - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

Aston Martin

Crawford was driving again in FP1 in place of Alonso. The rookie gave a good account of himself, beating Stroll for starters. Alonso returned to the cockpit in FP2, but immediately ran wide and damaged his car, leading to a stay in the pits. When he did come back out, he managed to beat his team mate as Stroll also ran wide, kicking up gravel as he skating off the track.

Fernando Alonso - FP2: 1:26.046, P19

Lance Stroll - FP1: 1:26.416, P20; FP2: 1:26.648, P20

Jak Crawford - FP1: 1:26.306, P19

Stroll said:

"It was a difficult day in Qatar.

"All the races have their own unique challenges and this is a very different circuit to Vegas, with much warmer temperatures. You're pushing in high-speed corners here and always trying to be on the edge.

"There are some things to work on tonight to try to get the car in a better window for this track."

Crawford said:

"It was a good practice session and probably my favourite one as well. The track here is pretty fun to drive in a Formula One car.

"It was a shame that Las Vegas FP1 didn't really happen for anyone due to the weather conditions, but I definitely feel like I've been learning about the car every time I've been out in it.

"There is a bit of work to do overnight to get the car in the best window."

Mike Krack, Chief Trackside Officer said:

"It was a tricky afternoon and evening of practice here in Qatar.

"It's a punishing high-speed corner circuit, with aggressive kerbs and gravel traps and we've seen a lot of cars going off track during both sessions.

"We've spent some time on repairs to both cars in between and during the sessions and we have some work to do overnight.

"It was good to see Jak get some more important mileage in the car during FP1 and Fernando then returned for FP2 and will continue for the remainder of the weekend."

Simone Berra, Pirelli Chief Engineer

"Qatar is once again proving to be the most demanding circuit of the season for the tyres. The race simulations carried out today, particularly during the second free practice session, confirmed expectations in terms of wear and degradation. Graining, encouraged by the dirty track surface and the level of aerodynamic load, was especially evident on the front-left tyre. This phenomenon accelerated tyre wear and led several tyres to reach very high levels of wear. It is a scenario that will make careful tyre management even more important for the teams ahead of Sunday’s race.

"Performance degradation also proved to be high, particularly on the front axle, to the extent that a two-stop strategy would probably have been the most competitive option even without the limitations introduced for this event to preserve tyre integrity. As for the compounds, the Soft proved competitive over a single lap, although some teams struggled to extract its full potential. The Hard was also noteworthy: despite being used by only a limited number of teams, it demonstrated remarkable consistency of performance. title: Verstappen and Red Bull left looking for car balance in Qatar
excerpt:
Max Verstappen admitted that he and Red Bull had "a bit of a difficult day" during Friday practice ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix.

The four-time World Champion was only able to finish P6 and P5 quickest across the two, one-hour sessions at the Lusail International Circuit, having struggled with understeer throughout the day.

"A bit of a difficult day. The balance of the car is just probably a bit too disconnected at the moment to go fast, so that’s what we need to fix," said Verstappen.

"The all-round balance is not there at the moment, so that is costing us quite a bit of lap time. We’ll keep trying and we’ll see how good we can get it."

Red Bull, along with other teams across the grid, were unable to match Mercedes over the course of the day, as Kimi Antonelli topped both sessions, with Verstappen stating "they look quite far ahead in the short run and long run".

Team mate Isack Hadjar also struggled with balance throughout, finishing P3 in Free Practice 1 before dropping to P6 later in the day.

Red Bull Technical Director Pierre Wache believes much more work is required to stand any chance of challenging Mercedes, but that he was unsure if the team would be able to close the deficit this weekend.

"It's clear that the car balance was a lot more understeery than expected during FP1 for both drivers, even more for Max than Isack but similar problem," he said.

"Tried to fix some problem, this problem for FP2. We didn't sort out fully, it went in the right direction, but with some compromise that was not ideal. We improve quite a lot the car but still a lot of work to do.

"Looks like they [Mercedes] are very, very strong in high speed corner. I didn't check their balance of the drive, but clearly on speed profile they look very strong and it will be a big challenge to match them.

"Try to concentrate on ourselves, fix our problem first and see where we are but I'm not very confident for tomorrow."

title: Racing Bulls lead midfield in Qatar after 'really big step'
excerpt:
Racing Bulls led the midfield pack after Friday practice ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix, as Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad finished Free Practice 2 in P9 and P10.

Both drivers hadn’t been entirely happy in FP1, but major changes – particular adding front wing to counter understeer – brought a significant improvement for the second session.

Despite the encouraging start to the weekend Lawson believes that there’s more to come ahead of Qualifying on Saturday at the Lusail International Circuit.

“We definitely didn't maximise," he said. "There's some stuff we can improve to put our lap together, just on some performance stuff. But overall, we have a strong car.

“We've just added a bit of rotation to the car. We had a bit too much understeer. I think if you'd have listened to almost any of the drivers – certainly we were listening to some – they were all complaining of the same thing.

“So understeer in that first session, and I suspect most people did something similar, to put more front end into the car for the second session.”

title: 'It's never nice' – Gasly explains dramatic FP2 spin
excerpt:
Pierre Gasly blamed low tyre temperatures for a dramatic spin that brought out the red flags during second practice for the Qatar Grand Prix.

The Alpine driver explained that his tyres had cooled during an earlier red-flag stoppage caused by gravel on the track, leaving him struggling for grip when the session resumed.

The lower pressures that resulted in turn led to his Alpine hitting the ground more, which caught him out and sent him spinning into a track marker board.

“It's never nice to find yourself facing the wrong way at such speeds,” said Gasly. “After the red flag, core temperatures, opening the lap I should probably not have gone for it. I was 10 degrees below the temperature, but I just thought get a feel for it.

“Low temperature, low pressure, so when I arrived there, the [Straight Mode] closed, I had more bottoming. And then it was the first time we're running a bit more power in the weekend, so came quite a lot faster than any other laps, and then eventually ran onto the kerb, bottomed out, and lost control of the car.

“So not great, but then it is what it is. Doesn't happen very often, so we'll try to get the learnings we can from the two sessions.”

Asked about damage, the Frenchman said: “Yeah, the floor, and I went so much into the gravel laterally, that probably had quite a lot of extra ballast in the car! But it will be fixed for tomorrow.”

Gasly was classified P12 in the session, having been P10 in FP1. He made it clear that tyre management will be key this weekend.

“It's a tough track,” Gasly said. “A lot of deg in FP1. Very tough for front tyres, and also the whole energy management around the track is having a lot more sort of impact than we think in terms of car balance, degradation, etcetera. So yeah, quite a lot to understand tonight.

“It's difficult to overtake, but based on the graining we've seen this morning, if it's the same on Sunday, then there are going to be big differences across the field.

“So I think most important is to get the balance in a better place. Still not fully pleased, and a lot of understeer around the lap. So hopefully we can find ways to just improve the balance for the rest of the weekend.”

Alpine Managing Director Steve Nielsen also pointed to the team's ongoing handling difficulties, suggesting that Gasly was not entirely to blame for the incident.

“Well, he's struggling with a very difficult car,” said Nielsen. “I think neither driver is very happy with the balance, and that shows us our pace, particularly in the high-speed. And Pierre's obviously pushing and got caught out. So, I wouldn't say it's all driver error.”

Regarding Gasly’s tyre temperature issue he said: “It's this new rule we have where red flag time gets added on. We weren't really expecting that, but there it is. We should learn to cope with it. So, I think that caught us out maybe a little bit, but yeah, just generally, the balance of the car is nowhere near where it needs to be.”

Nielsen also conceded that the car's long-standing weakness in high-speed corners is proving particularly costly in Qatar.

“We've made no secret of from the beginning," he added. "It comes and goes depending on circuit characteristics, combination of corners and temperatures and so on. But it's definitely hurting us here.”

title: Norris worried by McLaren’s deficit to Mercedes in Qatar
excerpt:
Lando Norris has admitted that McLaren could be fighting for P3 at best in Qatar with the Briton concerned by the team’s lack of pace relative to Mercedes despite an encouraging showing in Friday’s practice sessions.

Norris was third fastest during the second practice session at the Lusail International Circuit, finishing 0.445s adrift of Kimi Antonelli, with the Italian having set his fastest time on the medium tyres while the McLaren driver was on the softs.

With Mercedes having recorded a 1-2 in both of Friday’s sessions, Norris believes that McLaren are more closely matched with Red Bull and Ferrari heading into the remainder of the weekend.

“I don’t think we’re too bad relative to most, but to Mercedes, I don’t think we’ve been further off,” Norris admitted. “They just seem in a different category compared to us today, quicker in every single corner by a mile.

“So I would say the battle is for P3, and we seem in a relatively decent position. We seem similar in pace to Red Bull and similar-ish to Ferrari.

“There’s things we need to improve and things that can certainly be better. But I guess you always look to the top, so when you look at ourselves compared to Mercedes, we need to improve a lot everywhere.”

Having run an older specification of the MCL40’s floor on Friday, McLaren are set to switch to the newer version ahead of Saturday’s running, although Norris is doubtful that it will allow the team to take the challenge to the Silver Arrows.

“I don’t know how much [the new floor] will help around here, relative to Vegas, but I’ll see tonight and see how much we can gain from that,” he explained.

“It’s not going to be the gap that we need. I would say we’re around six, seven tenths, probably seven tenths off Mercedes a lap, so it’s not even worth thinking about them. I think relative to the rest, we seem like we’re in a good place. The fact that we can have the new floor tomorrow will add a little bit, but a little bit is always better than nothing.”

McLaren’s Racing Director, Randy Singh, explained that the decision to run the older floor specification on Friday was taken to protect the new floor from potential damage. The high speed corner characteristics of the Lusail International circuit can be brutal on the cars, and risk damaging floor components as drivers go over the kerbs on exit.

“Lots of high-speed corners here and some lower-speed corners, so getting the balance right is very tricky across the whole lap,” Singh explained.

“We ran the older-spec floor today, mostly just because you can see people running wide, damaging floors, and we didn’t want to damage any of the newer-spec floors. The new spec will be on tomorrow. It won’t be a massive difference, but it’s all small things that push us in the right direction.”

With Norris’ team mate Oscar Piastri finishing just 0.027s behind the Briton in fourth and Red Bull’s Max Verstappen a further 0.027s adrift in fifth, Singh is anticipating a closely fought Qualifying session.

“I think the top four teams will be close,” he added. “Maybe Mercedes will be a small step ahead. I think it’ll be very tight with us and Red Bull, and probably with Ferrari tomorrow.

“So it’s very hard to say putting the new floor on will do this or that, or even the changes we make overnight. I think it’s going to be tight, like it has been for this part of the season.”

title: Antonelli wary of rivals despite topping Friday in Qatar
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli believes "you can never write off Max [Verstappen] and the others" despite the new World Champion and Mercedes dominating Friday practice ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix.

The Italian topped both one-hour sessions at the Lusail International Circuit, leading Mercedes team mate George Russell both times as a gap emerged to the chasing pack.

This was also after both Antonelli and Russell failed to set a time in Free Practice 2 with the soft Pirelli tyre, suggesting their one-lap pace could be even greater come Qualifying on Saturday.

"I think it's going to be very close between me and George, then of course you can never write off Max and the others," said Antonelli.

"There's been already weekends where we were very strong in the beginning, then in Qualifying the others seem to make a big step and get close. We just need to keep working, keep improving and then we'll try to be ready for tomorrow."

Antonelli admitted that regardless of others catching up in terms of performance, it had been a strong day in Qatar.

Mercedes made several adjustments to the setup of the car throughout the day, with the high speed, flowing corners and warm conditions a stark contrast to Las Vegas the previous weekend.

"I think [it] was a productive day. I think we tried a lot of things on the car, also between FP1 and FP2," said Antonelli.

"FP2 seems like we did a step back with the car but [it] was very interesting to see how the car behaved after those changes and it's not easy. Long run, the front left is the one that is dropping, just need to find the right balance for Qualifying and then the race."

Sunday's 57-lap race will once again feature a unique rule, with tyre life for a set of tyres limited to just 27 laps, meaning all drivers will be required to make at least two stops.

Mercedes Deputy Team Principal Bradley Lord admitted that although having pace is the priority, ensuring that Antonelli and Russell can maintain tyre life will be critical if they are to succeed in the Grand Prix.

"I think the tyre duty is very much biased towards the left-hand side of the car, front and rear," he said.

"How you keep those tyres alive for what could be stints of up to 27 laps is a challenge. So one thing is pace, the other thing is long run, both pace and durability, and how you maybe need to throttle back a little bit in order to get the life out of the tyres. But so far, so good."

title: Audi's Italian GP appeal over Tsunoda decision is dismissed
excerpt:
Audi's appeal over a potential starting infraction at the Italian Grand Prix for Yuki Tsunoda has been dismissed following a hearing at the International Court of Appeal.

The incident in question came at Monza back in September, after Charles Leclerc's crash on the second lap. Tsunoda, who was making the second of three appearances for Racing Bulls this season, made a late change of direction into the correct grid box on the restart as he realised he was heading for the wrong grid position.

The drivers were sent round for a further formation lap before Tsunoda eventually finished in 10th to claim the final point on offer, with the driver not recieving a penalty.

This was due to several factors, according to the stewards at the time, primarily that "at no time was the team [Racing Bulls] advised that Race Control considered Car 22 to be the cause of the extra formation lap", and thus a pit lane start was not required.

Audi lodged an appeal against the decision, with drivers Gabriel Bortoleto and Nico Hulkenberg finishing P11 and P12 respectively.

Following a hearing of the International Court of Appeal (ICA) on 25 November, the FIA announced the decision on Friday with the Audi appeal dismissed.

The ICA found that "after having heard the parties and examined their submissions, [it] decided to declare the appeal admissible" and "dismiss the appeal on the merits", with the original result of the Italian Grand Prix standing.

It was also confirmed that "a full decision will be available at a later date".

title: Liam Lawson reveals 'big changes' behind Racing Bulls Qatar GP confidence spike
excerpt:
Liam Lawson claims "big changes" were made between practice sessions for the Qatar Grand Prix which have spiked confidence going into the remainder of the weekend.

Behind Mercedes, McLaren, Red Bull and Ferrari, Racing Bulls emerged as the leading team from a disjointed second practice at the Lusail International Circuit, disrupted by two red flags.

Lawson managed to get in a soft-tyre run before the first stoppage for a track clearance following an earlier trip into the gravel for Ferrari's Charles Leclerc that deposited stones and a part of his SF-26 on the track.

Arvid Lindblad completed most of a lap on the red-striped Pirellis before the red flags were shown, leaving his leading time on the mediums, albeit with him and Lawson 10th and ninth respectively on the timesheet behind the drivers from the 'big four' teams.

Asked whether he felt Racing Bulls was back to being the best of the rest, speaking to select media, including RacingNews365, Lawson said: "As a team, I think we are.

"We definitely didn't maximise. There's some stuff we can improve to put a lap together, just some performance stuff. But overall, we've got a strong car."

As to where the improvement was needed, he added: "Straight-line speed would do it. Let's obviously see tomorrow. We were really lacking it in P1, and we made a good step for P2. It's all stuff we can see and should be able to fix."

[Article continues below]

Lawson - 'They've ballooned'

Racing Bulls team principal Alan Permane, speaking to Sky Sports F1 during FP2, expressed confidence that the car was looking strong and reliable for the weekend.

Sharing Permane's enthusiasm, Lawson said: "We made a really big step with the car between the sessions. It's not often you make big changes over a race weekend, but we did, and the car was a lot better.

"We really had quite a good car in [F]P1, and now we have a faster car. We'll try and fine-tune it, but so far it's all worked."

The one area for concern for Lawson is the rise in tyre pressures for this weekend for safety reasons, given the high-speed nature of the circuit that has caused blowouts and punctures in the past.

For this race, as was the case last year, no set of tyres can run for more than 27 laps.

"The tyres feel very ballooned," remarked Lawson. "Obviously, it's for safety. It would be great to go down to some racier pressures that we used to run a long time ago.

"At the moment, it is what it is. It's going to make it hard for us in the race. Obviously, we have mandatory stops, so we're a bit constricted there anyway.

"Also, there's not a huge difference between the compounds, so it's going to be interesting, more for the race, I think.

"For us, we didn't run the C1 [hard]. I think only Gabi [Bortoleto] maybe ran it. We'll try and get a reference."

title: Lance Stroll reveals sudden health flare-up during Qatar practice
excerpt:
Lance Stroll has revealed he suffered from a sudden health issue during Qatar Grand Prix practice.

The Canadian, who placed 20th in both Friday sessions at the Lusail circuit, revealed that during the second session, he tweaked a muscle in his lower back through the high-speed sequence of corners towards the end of the lap.

Stroll had suffered a number of offs and through the gravel throughout the day, but confirmed that the issue with his back was not related to these.

The three-time podium-sitter will monitor the situation overnight, but conceded it was "bothering me a lot."

Should Stroll be unable to drive in the Qatar GP, the likely replacement for him would be Jak Crawford, who took Fernando Alonso's car in FP1 as the two-time champion stood down, and would thus make his grand prix debut.

"It was difficult. It's a different track to Las Vegas, and [I was] trying to put the car in a good window for this track, and then [I was] dealing with some back pain in the second session, so that was also really tricky," said Stroll, speaking to select media, including RacingNews365.

"I just tweaked my lower back in the second session, so I'm just battling that."

When then asked if the issue would "compromise" him for the rest of the weekend, Stroll explained that it would continue to be monitored.

"We're going to see," he said. "I'm going to try and work on it and do what I can tonight, but it was bothering me a lot."

Stroll had encountered several high-speed offs during the day, but confirmed the back issues were not caused by these.

"It wasn't actually in one of those offs," he said.

"It was just in the last sector, in the right-hand corner; it has just tweaked the lower back with the G-forces.

"[We'll] try to get on top of it tonight, and the car itself as well. There is a bit of damage to repair, and some things going on, so we're trying to put the car in a better window, and that's all I can really say."

title: Max Verstappen pinpoints specific area Red Bull must fix in Mercedes pursuit
excerpt:
Max Verstappen is seeking overnight improvements to remove the "disconnected" feeling he had during Friday practice at the Qatar Grand Prix.

Verstappen finished FP2 in fifth place, 0.4s behind the pace-setting Mercedes of Kimi Antonelli, with George Russell and both McLarens also ahead of the Dutch driver.

Verstappen finished 0.007s clear of team-mate Isack Hadjar as Red Bull placed firmly third fastest, but well ahead of the Ferraris, which did not get clean runs on the soft tyres.

The Red Bull driver has won every Qatar GP since it returned to the calendar in 2023, but feels the team requires a "big jump" if it is to reel in Antonelli and Russell to challenge at the top of the times.

"The steering was quite heavy. [We're] just not where we wanted to be, and it is a bit too disconnected at the moment," Verstappen said.

"We need to try and bring the balance together, and see if we can fix it for [for Saturday].

"It is a very different track, quite a unique track, and it is not an easy track to get things right, so I hope we can do a bit better.

"I think the gap to Mercedes is very big, so we need a big jump for that, and if we can get that balance more together, that's probably already half of the lap-time we're losing.

"[Mercedes] are properly quick on the straights, but also maybe have a bit nicer balance than we have at the moment.

"I mean, we're not happy ourselves, and when you are not happy yourself, it's very hard to get the same level."

title: Lewis Hamilton stoppage cements shocking Ferrari Qatar GP second practice
excerpt:
A late stoppage for Lewis Hamilton cemented a shocking second practice for Ferrari ahead of this weekend's Qatar Grand Prix.

title: Kimi Antonelli ends 14-race wait as two red flags hit Qatar GP practice
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli topped both Friday practice sessions for only the second time this season, albeit after a heavily disrupted FP2 ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix that was hit by two red flags.

Remarkably, Antonelli led the way at the Lusail International Circuit at the end of each session on Pirelli's medium compound. In FP2, in particular, he was unable to get in a soft-tyre run.

The session was stopped just before the half-hour mark for the first time to remove debris and sweep away gravel following a high-speed spin involving Ferrari's Charles Leclerc after just nine minutes.

Once the track was cleared, the second red flag appeared after three minutes when Pierre Gasly flew off the track at Turn 14, and beached his Alpine in the gravel.

Although the session was extended by 13 minutes to cover the time lost for the two interruptions, the teams and drivers naturally switched to long runs, as they would do under normal circumstances at the end of FP2.

That left Antonelli out in front with a lap of one minute 23.077s. It was the first time since the Austrian Grand Prix that the 20-year-old Italian had finished out front in the two Friday FPs.

There was still time for one final incident, though, when an engine issue forced Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton to pull off track in the closing minutes.

[Article continues below]

Ferrari woe and two stoppages

It was not long before Antonelli eased past his leading time from first practice, setting a time 0.140s quicker with a lap of 1:23.077s on the medium compound, at that stage a quarter of a second quicker than Russell.

On a following lap, Russell did at least edge closer to Antonelli, lowering the gap to 0.127s, with Verstappen then third quickest, over seven-tenths of a second adrift of Antonelli.

Red Bull duo Verstappen and Hadjar were the first to venture out on the soft tyres, yet the four-time F1 champion could draw no closer than half a second to Antonelli, with Hadjar seven-thousandths behind his team-mate.

McLaren duo Norris and Piastri both moved ahead of the Red Bull pair, but only marginally, leaving the outgoing champion 0.445s adrift of Antonelli, with the Australian 0.472s down.

That top six stayed static through to the end of the session given the stoppages. Russell was only seconds away from taking top spot when the stoppage occurred.

On his opening lap on the softs, Russell was three-tenths of a second up on Antonelli after the first two sectors, only to abort due to the first red flag caused by Leclerc's earlier spin that left a piece of his car on the circuit at Turn 12, and had taken time to spot by the FIA.

The session had only just started to get going again when Gasly exited after a further three minutes. When it resumed, there were only 15 minutes available at that point, with Leclerc, in particular, returning after a 38-minute delay.

Russell was not the only driver hampered by the stoppages, as many of his rivals failed to get in a soft-tyre, low-fuel sim.

That was despite FIA race director Rui Marquez extending the session to cater for the lost time across the two red flags, although there were no time improvements given the change in run plans.

There was a moment of note when Lewis Hamilton chopped across Verstappen as the seven-time F1 champion embarked on a fast lap, while his four-time counterpart was on a long run.

Verstappen moaned that the move was under braking, and although it was initially noted by the stewards, they opted not to hold a post-session investigation.

Hamilton's session still ended miserably with his late stoppage.

With the incidents for the Ferrari duo, behind the top six, they were both just over a second down, albeit on the mediums, followed by Red Bull duo Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad to round out the top 10, the latter on mediums, 1.470s down.

title: Qatar GP second practice suffers rapid back-to-back red flags
excerpt:
Second practice ahead of this weekend's Qatar Grand Prix has featured two red flags in close succession.

The first, with just under 30 minutes remaining in the session, was caused by debris on the circuit from Charles Leclerc's Ferrari, with the Monegasque having spun and subsequently spent 15 minutes in the garage.

Just moments after the session resumed, Alpine's Pierre Gasly had a much scarier moment, spinning at high speed in the final sector.

His car smashed through a polystyrene barrier and became beached in the gravel, resulting in a second red flag just minutes after the first.

The timing of the red flags severely impacted soft-tyre qualifying simulations. Mercedes had a one-two at the time of the second red flag.

title: Audi discover FIA Court of Appeal verdict over Italian Grand Prix
excerpt:
Audi has lost its appeal against the results of the 2026 Italian Grand Prix after the FIA's International Court of Appeal dismissed its case.

The German manufacturer appealed the results after Yuki Tsunoda caused an extra formation lap, yet still went on to line up 11th on the grid rather than start from the pit lane.

Audi appealed the results because Tsunoda, driving for Racing Bulls at the time, finished 10th, with Gabriel Bortoleto in P11, meaning a punishment for the Japanese driver would have earned Audi a point.

With its case having been dismissed, Audi must now cover the fees for the proceedings, which will be calculated and communicated to the Hinwil-based outfit at a later date.

Why the case has been dismissed will also be released at a later date, following the hearing which took place on November 25.

title: Sergio Perez learns stewards' verdict after unusual 22-minute absence
excerpt:
Sergio Perez has not been punished after arriving 22 minutes late for the second FIA drivers' press conference on media day ahead of this weekend's Qatar Grand Prix.

The Mexican had been scheduled to appear in the second of two press conferences at the Lusail International Circuit at 18:00 local time, alongside Oscar Piastri and Charles Leclerc.

However, the duo were left alone for 22 minutes before all questions had been asked and answered, allowing them to depart.

Twenty-two minutes after the scheduled start, Perez finally appeared on the press conference sofa and undertook a short solo press conference.

Usually, a punishment would be awarded, but not on this occasion. Perez escaped punishment after explaining that his flight landed late following an insurance issue and that his vehicle to the circuit was caught up by road closures.

The FIA stewards' report wrote: "The driver conceded that he was 22 minutes late for the press conference, however he explained that this was caused by two circumstances beyond his control. The first related to an insurance issue which resulted in his flight to Doha being delayed such that he landed only one hour prior to the scheduled start time for the conference. Normally this would have allowed him sufficient time to meet his commitment, however on approach to the circuit, he was held up by several road closures. The Stewards note that other parties were likewise held up on arrival at the circuit due to similar circumstances.

The team advised that it had kept the FIA media delegate informed of the delay.

Accordingly, although this is a breach of the regulations, in view of the circumstances, no penalty is applied.

title: Red Bull handed massive punishment after alarming Isack Hadjar incident
excerpt:
The F1 stewards have fined Red Bull €30,000 after an incident involving a practice stop for Isack Hadjar during FP1 at the Qatar Grand Prix.

During the session, Hadjar peeled into the pits for a front wing adjustment before being released seconds later.

However, as he got the signal to pull away, it was not safe to do so and he appeared to strike a mechanic with his left rear tyre before a colleague removed part of the cooling device that had become detached as Hadjar moved off.

Hadjar and Red Bull were summoned to the stewards under Article 12.2.1.h of the FIA International Sporting Code, which relates to team personnel being located in an unsafe position.

While Red Bull has been fined €30,000, two-thirds of the punishment has been suspended for 12 months unless a similar incident occurs.

Detailing their verdict, the stewards said: "The team representative explained that a new team member had placed a blower to cool the left rear brakes when in fact this was not normal procedure. Consequently the car commenced the pit box release procedure prior to the team member having removed the blower.

"This resulted in the car starting to leave the pit box with part of the blower still in place, and more importantly, the team member’s foot made contact with the rear left wheel of the car. This could have resulted in injury to the team member.

"The safety of team members during a pit stop is of the upmost importance irrespective of the session being free practice or a race. The team representative conceded that this was a procedural error on the part of the team.

"The penalty imposed is consistent with the penalties applied to similar incidents in recent years."

title: Kimi Antonelli sets daunting practice pace as Red Bull face stewards investigation
excerpt:
Check out the full report of all the action from Free Practice 1 ahead of the 2026 F1 Qatar Grand Prix.

Kimi Antonelli set a daunting early pace in the first practice session for the Qatar Grand Prix, as Red Bull is facing a post-session investigation.

The world champion set a blistering 1:23.217 on the medium tyres at the Lusail International Circuit - lapping faster on that compound than the rest of the field managed on the, in theory faster, soft compound tyres.

Antonelli did try his hand at a soft tyre lap, but could only post a 1:23.333 to go 0.116s slower - but still well ahead of team-mate George Russell, whose best time on the softs was 1:23.724 - 0.507s slower than the Italian.

In a session where the field largely struggled on the soft tyres, Isack Hadjar took third for Red Bull, with the McLarens the meat in a Red Bull sandwich with Max Verstappen down in sixth, nearly a second slower than Antonelli.

Ferrari was severely off the pace, with Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton 1.2s and 1.3s, respectively off the pace.

Red Bull is facing a post-session investigation from the stewards for an unsafe release of Hadjar from a practice pit-stop, where he appeared to hit a mechanic, who was uninjured.

Antonelli on the pace

In the first exchanges as dusk transitioned to night, Leclerc set the first representative lap time of 1:26.222, with Hamilton half-a-second slower before Antonelli immediately set out his stall with a 1:25.000 flat.

Russell was next through on a 1:25.273, as the Mercedes, Red Bulls and Ferraris used medium tyres whilst Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri took hards.

After more trading of lap-times, Antonelli whittled his down to a 1:24.057, and then a 1:23.731, and finally a 1:23.217 - which stood for the rest of the session.

Remarkably, drivers were largely unable to find chunks of time on the softs, with Leclerc's first attempt only finding 0.199s and Verstappen about four-tenths.

Russell got from a 1:23.978 to a 1:23.724 on the softs, but it was still not enough to challenge Antonelli's medium tyre time.

Antonelli's soft tyre lap was 1:23.333.

Verstappen struggled with understeer, and claimed he needed "10 clicks" of front-wing added in, whilst Hamilton also reported very high levels of degradation across his 26 laps in total.
